subject: Decision Making
title: Eisenhower and D-Day
description: Learn Eisenhower and D-Day in one minute.

hook.text: Eisenhower chose June 6, 1944 for D-Day based on a weather window. A wrong call would doom 150,000 soldiers.

buildup.text: The invasion needed low tides, full moons, and calm seas. Only a few days per month fit. June 5 was stormy.

discovery.text: One meteorologist saw a brief clearing on June 6. Eisenhower trusted the forecast and gave the order to go.

twist.text: He wrote a note taking full blame if the invasion failed. Leaders who own failure earn the right to decide.

climax.text: Eisenhower decided with incomplete data and irreversible stakes. That is the definition of leadership under uncertainty.

punchline.text: One weather window, 150,000 lives. Eisenhower decided and owned it.

quiz.question: What did Eisenhower prepare in case D-Day failed?
options: A note taking full personal blame for the failure
